b7uoi: A depiction of a female dancer coming through an ornate gold frame. Inspiration from an E.LEE painting created in 2018 for a show working with dancers from Hubbard Street. Painting is based off a photo of dancer Jacqueline Burnett
lry4i: A painting of two birds, one mechanical, and one not with a magical stone in the middle. This mural was created for ACTIVATE: a project of the Chicago Loop Alliance Foundation.
p256i: General idea is to honor the electrical workers by depicting the bending, positioning and angles that are required to manipulate the pipes for electricity. There's also the duality of male and female figures represented as professionals in their Craft/trade. The abstract piece in the middle is based on Tesla's AC/DC motor which he invented that allowed current to flow both ways; the patterns symbolize energy. The mural overall illustrates the human manipulation of energy and how we concentrate it for our own benefit and lighting the world.
lv57u: "First Responders" was designed by Jill Arena and painted by Cyd Smillie to commemorate the 10th anniversary of 9/11. It features the status of Liberty on a red background with a First Responder spraying a hose. It is on the south facing wall of 4508 N Miwaukee and on the day of its dedication the roll call for the firehouse across the street was held on site.
ics4i:
(Photo Credit: Sandra Steinbrecher) Brazilian artist, Eduardo Kobra specializes in “memory walls,” meaning that are specific to the community in which he is painting and evoke a certain nostalgia within the residents of that specific area. Chicago’s “memory wall” depicts legendary blues musician, Muddy Waters, was the perfect icon for this monumental wall.
The creation of this mural was a team effort and thanks go to several people, including Marc Realty, Beauty and Brawn Gallery & Think Space!
kkf56: Six Corners Association received a grant for the beautification of the Six Corners Business District. They passed that grant onto AAC with the goal of creating a mural for the 100' long brick wall on the west side of the 4935-37 Irving Park building. AAC contacted 5 local Artists and proposed a single mural on panels wherein each artist would showcase their trademark style in a somewhat loose narrative panorama. Penny Pinch, Shawnimals, Kathryn Eli, Carly Derec and Cyd Smillie each contributed to the mural.
izf2i: When scouting the location for her mural with Port Ministries, Artist Gloria Talamantes thought about the homeowners who refused buyouts for the Norfolk Southern railroad freight yard expansion in Englewood. Believing in the healing properties of flowers, she has incorporated flowers to surround people as they walk and ride by the mural.
8kcxu: "What we create" was funded in part thru an IAP grant from DCASE. It features what women do from house care and child care to creation to keeping dreams. The faces of the women are the faces of women in the community and Elizabeth Catlett on the far right. This mural was painted in part by the campers of I Grow Chicago.
h2el6: 1991, a mural designed by Olivia Gude and Marcus Akinlana with the assistance of the Youth Renaissance Mural Group, located at One Artist Rrow, and artisans' incubator building at 1809 E 71st Street. Black United Fund of Illinois bought the building in the 80's therefore we don't have the description, but we fo have a picture which I have attached.
idpsi: The Revival is an improv theater located at the site where the artform was invented in 1955 (see The Compass Players). The core philosophy of improv is known as "Yes And." This mural is an homage to the artform and features local community practitioners of improv.
